report: Reviewed the complete represented_completeness claim, the complete associated service_spec.rs implementation context, its single associated test, and the captured review policy. Requirements: (1) absent/unrepresented source must never become negative evidence; (2) symbols published by an incomplete phase may still establish their own positive facts; (3) omissions or unsupported source must not produce a false proof, failed lookup, or exhaustive ground No in any downstream consumer. These are universal completeness obligations, including propagation across phase/consumer boundaries, not merely permission to retain a symbol list. The only implementation entry is explicitly in sage_meta::todo: uniform restriction/completeness accounting is not yet enforced at every semantic boundary. This adequately declares the common missing prerequisite for all three obligations: complete phase accounting and downstream propagation of incomplete/ambiguous outcomes while preserving individually represented positive facts. There is no ordinary implementation evidence and no claim of implementation completeness. The sole associated test, todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_represented_completeness, has an empty executable body and explicit TODO comments; it is correctly deferred, not a meaningful passing assertion. Its planned malformed, unresolved, unsupported-attribute and resource-limited scenarios address distinct ways source may be unavailable, require surviving usable represented symbols, and require potentially affected resolution/solver-negative queries to stay incomplete or ambiguous. This test depends on the missing uniform phase and consumer completeness behavior identified immediately above it. When implemented, those fixtures must exercise both positive retained facts and each forbidden negative outcome (false proof, failed lookup, exhaustive ground No); the present TODO does not establish any of them. A consumer converting an unsupported omission into a definitive missing lookup would not be detected by the empty body, which is precisely why the existing TODO classification must remain. No N/A or ordinary entries are present, and there are no helpers used by the placeholder to capture. All requirements are accounted for by explicit accepted deferral; no implementation or regression fix is asserted. Commands actually executed were review start with captured coordinator instructions and review read for the review policy; no behavioral tests were run because the only associated test has no executable assertions. This approval accepts the honest deferred status only and does not assert that the semantic guarantee currently holds.
